preamble: The alveolar lateral approximant [l] is realized as the voiced retroflex flap [ɽ], losing lateral airflow and gaining a retroflex tap. The documented case is Kanuri (Saharan), where /l/ surfaces as [ɽ] before /i/ (/báli/ 'tomorrow' [báɽi]); Cyffer argues the rule is old, since Kanuri loans into neighbouring Chadic languages reflect it as r.

examples.note: Synchronic allophony: Kanuri /l/ is realized as the retroflex flap [ɽ] before /i/ (/l/ → [ɽ] / _i). Cyffer argues the rule is older than Kanuri consonant weakening, since Kanuri loans in Ngizim, Bade and Karekare reflect it as r (Ngizim zōrí 'fool', Bade rītərîn 'Monday').
Before vowels other than /i/ the lateral stays [l]: lâdə 'Sunday', bígəla 'harvest season'.

sources: Cyffer, N. (2006). Kanuri and its neighbors: When Saharan and Chadic languages meet. Studies in African Linguistics 35. https://doi.org/10.32473/sal.v35i0.107315
